correctness.rationale: The all-prime-power proof is purely algebraic and complete. The projective-point incidence Gram is aI+bJ with a=Br(v-r)/(v(v-1))>0, proving dimension [n]_q. Restriction to the point-star identifies the full quotient projective-incidence subspace of rank [n-1]_q because each nonfixed point projects to exactly one quotient point with q lifts. Two-transitivity of GL(n-1,q) makes its mean-zero permutation constituent irreducible, so the compressed operator has just the constants and one nontrivial eigenvalue; 1_A is itself a bandlimited point-incidence function and has eigenvalue 1. Trace of the compressed operator equals [k]_q and gives theta=([k]_q-1)/([n-1]_q-1)=[k-1]_q/[n-2]_q. The nullity is [n]_q-[n-1]_q=q^(n-1), including the top-degree degeneracy. Standard singular-value equivalence supplies the interpolation norm. The packaged checker constructs actual projective incidence matrices for 11 parameter combinations with q=2,3,4, checks all multiplicities, and has max eigenvalue error under 5e-15; these finite numerical calculations are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: Claim-implication comparison: the 2004 Radon-transform theorem supplies GL-equivariant global kernels; its statements are on the full Grassmann homogeneous space and have no fixed-point window, so its asserted conclusions do not include the complete Schubert-star compression eigenvalues or sampling singular values. The 2013 global orthogonal-basis theorem has no spatial concentration operator; deriving the present exact multiplicity and conditioning requires new point-stabilizer restriction and trace steps. The 2004 continuous-sphere Slepian theory motivates the question but has a different space and geometry. An exact global first-idempotent endpoint norm would concern matrix row sums, which do not imply a spatially compressed Hilbert-space spectrum. No equivalent or dominating statement was identified by the recorded exact formula, projective incidence, principal-angle, and concentration searches; this is evidence-bounded, not global novelty certification.

value.rationale: The first nonconstant Grassmann spherical band and the one-point Schubert star are canonical finite-harmonic counterparts of a Slepian bandlimit and spatial window. The theorem gives a natural complete spectral classification uniformly in every prime-power field size and subspace dimension, with only one intermediate concentration eigenvalue, exact rank independent of k, q^(n-1) exact nullity independent of k, and sharp sampling/interpolation conditioning. The finite-field quotient incidence and parabolic symmetry are essential; this is not a bare textbook norm identity, arbitrary numerical cutoff, or reparameterization of a previously accepted theorem. The exact interpolation cost also quantifies the unavoidable information loss on star samples.
